correctness.rationale: An ordered deletion is uniquely specified by its weakly increasing source-copy indices t_i. For the j-th rank of surviving copies of each letter, the letters deleted by copy j form an initial segment of length h_j. The surviving block uses the tail of copy j and the head of copy j+1 in that order. Weak monotonicity of h_j orders adjacent blocks and the first-crossing construction inverts the encoding. Reduction of h_j modulo q only identifies 0 and q. With a nonzero phase in the output the lift is unique; the all-zero phase word has exactly r+1 lifts. Subtracting r from the embedding count yields the stated cardinality, including r=0. The bounded independent replay /workspace/replay_frozen.py 3 confirms 48 full-fiber and language comparisons, using a transfer over the source periods.
residual_risks: Finite replay alone does not establish unbounded q or r; the proof supplies the universal quantifiers.

evidence: Each nonterminal deletion gap is its least required phase increment plus q times a nonnegative integer; the terminal gap uses the remaining budget. With budget q, E_q>0 leaves no whole period to assign, hence the output has one embedding. E_q=0 is exactly P^r; its entire deleted period can be placed in any of r+1 gaps.
